title: what does the reference ring already contain?
subtitle: reference bias is already included in the configured resonance and loss

title: how much light reaches the next ring?
subtitle: equal supplied spacing and power attenuation; chip input loss handled upstream; final segment unmodeled

title: how does warming move the resonance?
subtitle: quadratic wavelength tuning; the slope anchor and reference resonance temperature need not coincide

title: what changes when we rebase the thermal law?
subtitle: same quadratic curve and curvature; only the expansion point and coefficient representation change

title: what does reverse bias change physically?
subtitle: voltage tables describe carrier-dependent index, absorption, capacitance, and resistance; fill fraction scales the junction-covered length

title: how does a voltage become device properties?
subtitle: piecewise-linear interpolation; values outside the table hold the endpoint and flag clipping; the reference index and loss are subtracted downstream

title: how do heat and bias move the same resonance?
subtitle: thermal and electrical shifts are added; the reference bias contribution is already in the original resonance

title: which optical loss becomes heat?
subtitle: two temperature sensitivities scale total intrinsic loss; nonabsorptive loss stays fixed; negative loss and invalid heat shares are clamped

title: where does a fixed laser sit on the shifted phase curve?
subtitle: translate the reference phase curve; the physical laser wavelength stays fixed; reference phase already includes coupler phase

title: what wavelength dependence does the reference curve retain?
subtitle: quadratic effective-index expansion and linear group-index expansion about the reference wavelength; these are local wavelength approximations, not time integration

title: what does sharing the level-zero delay mean?
subtitle: the two voltage cases can sample different group indices; only the level-zero group delay is retained for both

title: which inputs differ between zero and one?
subtitle: same instantaneous temperatures; separate voltage-dependent outputs; probability weighting occurs later in optics.py

title: why can wavelength change coupling?
subtitle: evanescent overlap motivates wavelength dependence; this picture holds geometry and index factors fixed to isolate the tail mechanism

title: how does power transfer along a coupler?
subtitle: ideal phase-matched lossless uniform coupler; power exchanges sinusoidally with distance and can return to the launch guide

title: why does runtime coupling use a local exponential?
subtitle: first-order approximation to logarithmic wavelength dependence; matches reference value and slope, but omits changing relative slope

title: what does sliding every resonance together miss?
subtitle: all orders receive one wavelength shift; a fuller thermal-dispersion model also changes spacing; anchoring one order does not verify the others

title: how do the phase.py calculations connect?
subtitle: this is an input-assembly map, separate from the physical schematics; time advancement belongs to thermal.py and selfheat.py
